messages:
Alex (Support): filing here — ACME reported 5xx + high p99 (~2s) on requests that should be served from APAC. They see auth failures and redirects to eu-west. ticket: #12345, customer is pretty upset.
Maya (eng-oncall): can you paste a sample request/response pair and request-id?
Alex (Support): sent in ticket but pasting minimal repro: 
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer tk_acme_abc" -H "X-Client-Region: apac" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
# response: 401 Unauthorized, via: eu-west, x-request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d
```
Alex (Support): they also saw spikes in billing events (duplicate charge attempts) on retries.
Julian (eng-runtime): looking at routing logs for rq_0a1b2c3d — request came into apac edge, routing decision did fallback to eu-west due to transient capacity signal from apac pool. Fallback logic then attempted sticky session to eu-west for same client-id. However, eu-west runtime rejected KV lookup for token namespace -> auth failure.
Priya (eng-sre): logs show: `route_decision: fallback(eu-west) reason=pool_egress_full ttl_mismatch=120s` then `kv_get(token_namespace): miss` and `auth: token_not_found` — appears KV namespace mapping is region-scoped; sticky routing moved session but didn't copy token namespace.
Maya (eng-oncall): so root cause = fallback routing + region-scoped KV auth; the client had a session pinned to apac but fallback routed them without token replication.
Chloe (Product): ACME says they get charged on retries even though final response was 401. Which component emits billing events?
Julian (eng-runtime): billing events emitted when request accepted by a worker (before auth check in our flow). Retry logic in the client plus our retries produced multiple accept events. We should treat auth fails as no-bill in fallback window until auth validated.
Priya (eng-sre): immediate mitigation: disable cross-region fallback for sessions with active auth tokens (config flag) and add fast failover to local-only when KV miss occurs. I can flip the feature flag for apac now.
Maya (eng-oncall): please do and confirm. Also create a whitelist to unblock ACME while we investigate.
Priya (eng-sre): flipping flag in console... done. routing table refreshed.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created and linked to #12345 — severity=sev2.
Alex (Support): ACME confirmed failures stopped ~30s after flag flip and no new billing duplicates observed. They're still asking for postmortem.
Julian (eng-runtime): followups: (1) change billing pipeline to delay emission until auth success (owner: billing infra), (2) update fallback to copy/lookup tokens or avoid fallback for session tokens (owner: runtime), (3) add observability for route-fallback -> kv-miss chains (owner: eng-sre).
Chloe (Product): add rollback policy for cross-region fallback in 2-week rollout; customers should opt-in for cross-region sticky sessions.
Maya (eng-oncall): quick repro steps for engineering: 1) create token scoped to apac, 2) simulate apac capacity decline, 3) send requests with X-Client-Region: apac and observe fallback to eu-west, 4) check `kv_get(token_namespace)` and billing events. Use request id prefix `rq_test_fallback`.
Alex (Support): I notified ACME of mitigation and that we'll refund duplicate charges if any were billed. They want ETA for fix.
Julian (eng-runtime): ETA for a proper fix (token-aware fallback + safe-billing) = 2 sprints. We'll provide interim guardrails next week.
Chloe (Product): I'll draft customer comms and a short postmortem summary for legal/finance.
Maya (eng-oncall): assigning owners in tracker: runtime@julian, sres@priya, billing@team-billing, product@chloe.
Alex (Support): thanks — keeping ticket open until postmortem published and ACME confirms refund. :thumbsup:
